flashcard_questions.q: Which chart did a medieval physician consult to decide the best time to treat a patient?
What did a medieval physician examine, then compare against a chart, to find the humour out of balance?
Which bloodletting method used a sharp blade to cut open a vein?
Which bloodletting method used heated glass cups to draw blood to the surface?
What did medieval doctors give a patient to force vomiting and remove excess humours?
Which herbal remedy contained salicin, the chemical the body converts into the active ingredient of aspirin?
Who performed surgery in medieval England instead of university-trained physicians?
Which of the three great problems of medieval surgery could not be solved because surgeons could not seal blood vessels?
What did medieval surgeons mean by 'laudable pus'?
flashcard_questions.a: The belief that pus forming in a wound was a good sign of healing.

flashcard_questions.q: Who was the Islamic surgeon from Cordoba known as the 'Father of Modern Surgery'?
How many new surgical instruments did Abulcasis invent?
Which two surgeons at Bologna used wine on wounds and rejected the idea of 'laudable pus'?
What did John of Arderne use to relieve pain during operations?
Who invented a screw-like tool to pull an arrowhead from the future Henry V's skull?
Public dissection was first allowed at the University of Bologna in ____.

notes: 14 cards: 2 diagnosis, 3 treatment terms, 5 person-to-significance, 1 figure, 1 cloze on a date. Dropped minor glossary terms (anal fistula detail, trepanning) as flavour.
